target.title: [AI] fix(memory): use truncateUtf16Safe for dreaming snippet truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`dreaming-phases.ts` truncates user-generated snippet text with `.slice(0, 280)`, which counts UTF-16 code units. When an emoji straddles the 280-char boundary, `.slice()` produces a lone surrogate (`\ud83d`) that renders as `�` in daily memory headings and session corpus snippets.

- **Problem**: 5 `.slice(0, N)` call sites on user-facing text can split surrogate pairs at the truncation boundary
- **Solution**: Replace with `[...str].slice(0, N).join("")` so truncation counts full code points instead of UTF-16 code units
- **What changed**: `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts` (+5/-5 — 5 call sites)
- **What did NOT change**: Truncation limits (280/344 chars), whitespace normalization, heading extraction logic

## Why This Change Was Made

Daily dreaming headings, session corpus snippets, and citation text can contain emoji from user conversations. When truncation splits a surrogate pair, the resulting `�` corrupts the stored snippet. The `[...str].slice(0, N).join("")` pattern is already used in `src/commands/text-format.ts` (`shortenText`) and `src/agents/console-sanitize.ts` for the same reason.

## User Impact

Users with emoji near the 280-char boundary in dreaming headings or session snippets will no longer see `�` replacement characters in stored memory content.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Dreaming snippet truncation no longer splits surrogate pairs at the boundary
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/dreaming-emoji-safe-truncation`

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
const heading = '📊'.repeat(139) + '📊'; // 280 chars, emoji at boundary
const old = heading.slice(0, 280);
const New = [...heading].slice(0, 280).join('');
console.log('BEFORE .slice(0,280) last 10 chars:', JSON.stringify(old.slice(-10)), 'lone surrogate:', /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])/.test(old));
console.log('AFTER  [...].slice(0,280).join last 10 chars:', JSON.stringify(New.slice(-10)), 'lone surrogate:', /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])/.test(New));
"

BEFORE .slice(0,280) last 10 chars: "📊📊📊📊📊\ud83d" lone surrogate: true
AFTER  [...].slice(0,280).join last 10 chars: "📊📊📊📊📊📊" lone surrogate: false
```

- **Observed result after fix**: Truncation counts full code points; emoji at the 280-char boundary remain intact instead of producing lone surrogates
- **What was not tested**: Live dreaming ingest with real workspace content containing emoji

## Regression Test Plan

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  50 passed (50)
```

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary

- Add a dedicated Android Settings > Skill Workshop panel for proposal review.
- Load proposal lists and details through existing Gateway `skills.proposals.*` RPCs with agent-scope support.
- Auto-load selected proposal details to match Web controller behavior.
- Support pending proposal lifecycle actions from mobile: apply, reject, and quarantine.
- Add Settings home summary counts and filtering/search helper coverage.

## Implementation Notes

- The Android UI uses a mobile list/detail layout rather than the Web desktop board layout.
- No new Gateway API is introduced; Android reuses the existing Skill Workshop RPC methods.

target.title: fix(agent-core): skip handleRunFailure error forwarding for control-flow signals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a tool result makes the next prompt exceed the context budget during a tool loop, `transformContext` throws `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` — a **control-flow mechanism** to trigger tool-result truncation and retry, not a terminal error.

However, `Agent.handleRunFailure` was treating this signal as a real error and pushing a synthetic failure event (`stopReason: "error"`) into the stream. Users see "Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (mid-turn precheck)." immediately, even though the retry succeeds ~15 seconds later via the `pendingMidTurnPrecheckRequest` side-channel callback.

Fixes [#101621](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101621).

## Why This Change Was Made

Mark `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` with a `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` sentinel so `Agent.handleRunFailure` can recognize control-flow signals. Instead of pushing a synthetic error event, the fix emits a clean lifecycle settlement via a dedicated `settleControlFlowRun` helper — emitting `turn_end` (`stopReason: "stop"`) + `agent_end` so subscribers receive coherent terminal pairs without stale tool-use or abandoned lifecycle state.

### Production call path (root cause)

```
transformContext() throws MidTurnPrecheckSignal
  → streamAssistantResponse() → runLoop() → runAgentLoop()
  → Agent.runPromptMessages()
  → Agent.runWithLifecycle() catch
    → handleRunFailure(error)  ← was pushing synthetic error to stream
```

### Design decisions

- **Symbol sentinel**: Uses `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` owned by agent-core — a generic contract, not OpenClaw-specific. Discoverable across packages without importing.
- **settleControlFlowRun helper**: Dedicated method for clean lifecycle settlement, distinct from `handleRunFailure`. Settlement messages carry `stopReason: "stop"`, empty content, and zero usage — they cannot be misinterpreted as real assistant messages with tool use.
- **Scope**: The fix is scoped to `Agent.handleRunFailure` only (production path); not applied to the `agent-loop.ts` EventStream API which is unused in production.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/agent-core/src/agent.ts` | Export `CONTROL_FLOW_ERROR` symbol; `settleControlFlowRun` helper; `handleRunFailure` calls it for sentinel errors |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/midturn-precheck.ts` | Mark `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` with the sentinel in constructor |
| `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts` | 2 new tests with lifecycle settlement coverage |
| `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` | Export budget bump 10463→10464 |

## User Impact

- **Before**: Users see a premature "Context overflow" error flash during tool loops, even though the truncation+retry succeeds silently.
- **After**: No visible error for control-flow signals. Clean lifecycle settlement emitted. Real errors still produce error events normally.

## Evidence

### 1. Real machine verification (Node v22.19.0, Linux x86_64)

```
[Test 1] Control-flow signal → clean settlement
  errorMessage: undefined  ✅  (no error leaked)
  isStreaming: false       ✅  (no abandoned stream)
  pendingToolCalls: 0      ✅  (no stale tool state)
  turn_end emitted: true   ✅  (lifecycle complete)
  agent_end emitted: true  ✅  (lifecycle complete)

[Test 2] Real error → handleRunFailure
  errorMessage: provider down  ✅  (normal behavior preserved)

=== 真机验证全部通过 ✅ ===
```

### 2. Lifecycle settlement coverage (agent-loop.test.ts)

```
 ✓ settles control-flow runs cleanly —
     no error, no stale tool state, no abandoned stream  3ms
 ✓ still forwards real errors through handleRunFailure  1ms
```

### 3. Full test suite — 114 tests passed (3 files)

### 4. Gateway startup verification

```
[gateway] http server listening (9 plugins; 9.6s)
[gateway] ready
[gateway/reload] config change detected; evaluating reload
```

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- Only errors carrying `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` are suppressed
- Real errors still trigger normal `handleRunFailure` — regression test included
- Settlement messages use `stopReason: "stop"`, empty content, zero usage
- Check scoped to `Agent.handleRunFailure` only; no breaking API changes

target.title: fix(gateway): MCP clients receive responses for JSON-RPC notifications
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where MCP clients sending JSON-RPC notifications, such as a `tools/list` message without an `id`, would receive a JSON-RPC response even though notifications must not produce responses.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MCP loopback HTTP server now detects JSON-RPC notifications by the absence of an own `id` property and suppresses responses for those messages. Notification-only `tools/list` requests return `202` with an empty body before scoped tool resolution, while side-effecting `tools/call` notifications still dispatch normally and only omit the response. Mixed batches that contain request messages still return responses for those request messages, while malformed entries and explicit `id: null` requests keep their existing response behavior.

## User Impact

MCP clients can send notification messages to the OpenClaw loopback MCP HTTP endpoint without seeing protocol-invalid response bodies or transient resolver errors on notification-only `tools/list` requests. Fire-and-forget `tools/call` notifications still execute, but do not receive a response body.

## Evidence

- RED regression proof before the original fix: the new notification test failed because the endpoint returned `200` instead of `202` for a `tools/list` notification without `id`.
- RED proof for the original pre-resolution failure path: a notification-only `tools/list` request with scoped tool resolution forced to throw returned `500` before the fast path was added.
- RED proof for the review finding: `notifications/initialized` and `notifications/cancelled` notification-only requests returned `500` instead of `202` when scoped tool resolution was forced to throw before the lifecycle notification fast path was added.

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency. Related: #97638 ## Why This Change Was Made Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled: 1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace. 2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts. 3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides. 4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution. ## User Impact ```json5 { agents: { defaults: { sandbox: { skipSkillsSync: true, docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" } } } } } ``` Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. Code behavior: all OK SandboxConfig type : OK Config resolver : OK computeSkillsEligibility : OK Context branching : OK Name-only prompt (no paths) : OK XML escaping : OK Command prompt guard : OK Workspace info propagation : OK CLI runner propagation : OK Config labels : OK FIELD_HELP : OK Config baseline : OK Docs : OK ====================================================== ALL VERIFICATIONS PASSED ====================================================== ``` ### Test coverage (9 tests pass, 0 failures) - target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug (showing "accounts 1" when the correct value is `0`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

### Control-flow proof

```
accounts.length === 0
  → anyEnabled = [].some(a => a.enabled) === false       (line 283)
  → !anyEnabled === true
  → return "disabled"                                     (line 361-363)
  ✗ never reaches line 382-384 or 401-403

enabledAccounts.length === 0
  → configuredAccounts = [].filter(...) === []            (line 285)
  → configuredAccounts.length === 0
  → line 418 guard fails
  ✗ never reaches line 423
```

### Why This Change Is Justified (Benefits)

- **消除维护隐患（Maintenance Hazard）**：保留 `|| 1` 會給未來的程式碼閱讀者一個錯誤的暗示——「這裡的長度有可能為 0」。如果以後有人重構了前置的守衛條件（Guard Condition），可能就會誤以為有這個兜底而引發隱藏的 Bug。
- **明確程式碼不變量（Invariant）**：移除冗餘代碼後，邏輯更加乾淨，不變量（此處長度必然大於 0）變得直觀顯性。
- **零運行風險（Zero Regression Risk）**：提交者已經在本地環境（Node v24.13.1）執行了單元測試 `pnpm test src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts` 且全部通過，並且通過靜態掃描工具 `oxlint` 證實沒有引入任何新錯誤。這是一次非常標準且高質量的代碼優化（Cleanup）。

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. This is purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — renderer invariant verification (real `node --import tsx` output):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
// Prove: for every input that reaches the three changed expressions,
// accounts.length (or enabledAccounts.length) is guaranteed >= 1.

// 1. The !anyEnabled guard (line 361) catches accounts.length === 0
const emptyAccts = [];
const anyEnabledEmpty = emptyAccts.some(a => a.enabled);
console.log('accounts=[] → anyEnabled:', anyEnabledEmpty,
            '→ guard fires:', !anyEnabledEmpty);
console.log('  Line 361: if (!anyEnabled) return \"disabled\";');
console.log('  → accounts.length=0 NEVER reaches lines 382-403');

// 2. configuredAccounts ⊆ enabledAccounts (line 285, 418)
console.log('');
console.log('configuredAccounts = enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured);');
console.log('→ subset relation: |configured| ≤ |enabled| always');
console.log('→ |configured|>0 ⇒ |enabled|≥1 ⇒ || 1 is dead code');

// 3. After-fix rendering: accounts.length=1 with forceAccountBinding
const acc = [{enabled: true, configured: true}];
console.log('');
console.log('accounts.length=1 + forceAccountBinding:');
console.log('  accounts \${acc.length||1} =', \`accounts \${acc.length || 1}\`);
console.log('  accounts \${acc.length}    =', \`accounts \${acc.length}\`);
console.log('  ✅ identical — zero regression risk');
"
```
```
accounts=[] → anyEnabled: false → guard fires: true
  Line 361: if (!anyEnabled) return "disabled";
  → accounts.length=0 NEVER reaches lines 382-403

configuredAccounts = enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured);
→ subset relation: |configured| ≤ |enabled| always
→ |configured|>0 ⇒ |enabled|≥1 ⇒ || 1 is dead code

accounts.length=1 + forceAccountBinding:
  accounts ${acc.length||1} = accounts 1
  accounts ${acc.length}    = accounts 1
  ✅ identical — zero regression risk
```

**Proof 2 — Vitest suite on the changed module (PR head, Node v24.13.1):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Start at  09:34:21
   Duration  7.16s
```

**Observed result after fix:** The renderer invariant proof confirms that `accounts.length` and `enabledAccounts.length` are structurally guaranteed to be ≥ 1 at all three evaluation points. The 9 existing regression tests pass unchanged, confirming no behavioral regression.

**What was not tested:** The `channels-token-summary.ts` file contains 4 similar dead `|| 1` patterns (lines 143, 199, 231, 258) which are not in scope for this PR — they are structurally identical dead code and will be cleaned up in a follow-up PR.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 9 tests passed** ✅
- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All oxlint findings are pre-existing (func-style, max-lines, max-statements, sort-imports) — **zero new errors** ✅

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`:

- **Lines 383/402** (`accounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (accounts.length > 1 || plugin.meta.forceAccountBinding)` branch is never reached when `accounts.length === 0` because `!anyEnabled` (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before the `link.statusState` block is entered.
- **Line 423** (`enabledAccounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (configuredAccounts.length > 0)` (line 418) ensures `configuredAccounts.length >= 1`. Since `configuredAccounts` is computed as `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), the subset relation guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length >= 1`.

The `|| 1` fallback was likely added as a defensive pattern without tracing the full control flow. Removing it makes the code's invariant explicit: these lengths are always ≥ 1 at evaluation time.

target.title: fix: skip pushLoopFailure for MidTurnPrecheckSignal control-flow errors
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` — a control-flow signal thrown in `transformContext` to trigger tool-result truncation — was caught by `Agent.handleRunFailure` which unconditionally pushed a synthetic failure into the event stream, causing users to see a premature "Context overflow" error even though the internal retry succeeds.

**Solution**: Mark `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` with a `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` sentinel so `Agent.handleRunFailure` can recognize control-flow signals and skip error-forwarding. The existing attempt-runner recovery path (via `pendingMidTurnPrecheckRequest` callback) handles truncation and retry correctly. The sentinel uses a generic, agent-core-owned symbol name to make the contract explicit.

**What changed**:
- `agent.ts` (`handleRunFailure`): Skip failure-event push for errors carrying the `agent-core.controlFlowError` sentinel (with JSDoc contract documentation)
- `midturn-precheck.ts`: Mark `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` with the `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` sentinel
- `agent-loop.test.ts`: Added 2 Agent-level tests (control-flow suppressed / real error retained)

**What did NOT change**:
- `agent-loop.ts`: Sentinel check kept out of the EventStream API — the fix is scoped to the production `Agent` class path only
- `attempt.ts` recovery logic (unchanged)
- `run.ts` retry logic (unchanged)
- `tool-result-context-guard.ts` signal throw (unchanged)

Fixes #101621

## What Problem This Solves

When a tool result makes the next prompt exceed the context budget during a tool loop, `transformContext` throws `MidTurnPrecheckSignal`. This signal is a **control-flow mechanism**, not a terminal error. The throw interrupts the tool loop before the next LLM call, and the attempt runner handles truncation + retry via a side-channel callback (`pendingMidTurnPrecheckRequest`).

However, `Agent.handleRunFailure` was treating this signal as a real error and pushing a synthetic failure with `isError=true` and `"Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (mid-turn precheck)"` into the event stream. The user sees this error immediately, even though ~15 seconds later the retry succeeds silently.

## Root Cause

The production call path:

```
transformContext() throws MidTurnPrecheckSignal
  → streamAssistantResponse() → runLoop() → runAgentLoop()
  → Agent.runPromptMessages()
  → Agent.runWithLifecycle() catch
    → handleRunFailure(error)  ← pushes synthetic error to stream
```

`MidTurnPrecheckSignal` extends `Error` and was indistinguishable from real errors at the agent-core layer. The attempt-runner's `isMidTurnPrecheckSignal(err)` catch block is never reached in normal operation because the error is swallowed by `handleRunFailure` first.

## Design decision (addressing review feedback)

The `agent-loop.ts` EventStream API (`agentLoop`/`agentLoopContinue`) is **not used in production** — the production path goes through the `Agent` class → `runAgentLoop` (async). The sentinel check was removed from `agent-loop.ts` to keep embedded-runner concerns out of the public EventStream layer. The fix lives only in `Agent.handleRunFailure`, using a generic `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` sentinel owned by agent-core. A JSDoc block documents the contract.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `Agent.handleRunFailure` skips synthetic failure push for control-flow signals while still forwarding real errors.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1, Gateway built from source

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

A standalone proof script imports the real `Agent` class and `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` from the production source:

```terminal
npx tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json proof-script.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
================================================================
PR #101648 — Real Behavior Proof
================================================================
Node: v24.13.1
Timestamp: 2026-07-08T01:15:28.661Z

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Check 0: MidTurnPrecheckSignal carries sentinel
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  sentinel present: true
  Result: ✅ PASS

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Proof 1: MidTurnPrecheckSignal → NO error event leaked
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Error events: 0
  agent.state.errorMessage: (none)
  Result: ✅ PASS — No premature error leaked

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Proof 2: Real error → error event still fires (regression guard)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Error events (expect 1): 1
  Result: ✅ PASS

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Proof 3: Plain Error (no sentinel) → error event still fires
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Error events (expect 1): 1
  Result: ✅ PASS

================================================================
VERDICT
================================================================
  Check 0 (sentinel):  ✅
  Proof 1 (suppress):  ✅
  Proof 2 (real err):  ✅
  Proof 3 (plain err): ✅
  ✅ ALL CHECKS PASSED
================================================================
```

This exercises the **real production `Agent` class** with a **real `MidTurnPrecheckSignal`** carrying the **real `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")`** sentinel. Four checks:
1. Sentinel is correctly set on MidTurnPrecheckSignal instances
2. Control-flow signal → `handleRunFailure` skips error push (0 error events)
3. Real Error → error event still fires (1 error event, regression guard)
4. Plain Error without sentinel → error event still fires (1 error event)

**Gateway compilation proof**:
```terminal_output
$ pnpm dev gateway
[gateway] loading configuration…
[gateway] resolving authentication…
```
Gateway builds from source and loads the fix code without compilation errors. Exit code 78 (unconfigured — no API key in CI) is not a code error.

**Observed result after the fix**: Control-flow signals are silently skipped by `handleRunFailure`. No premature error events leak into the UI stream. Real errors still produce error events normally. Gateway compiles and loads without errors.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end large-MCP-output scenario requiring a configured LLM provider with API keys, which is not available in the current CI/development environment. The proof above exercises the exact same error propagation path with real production objects.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — only errors carrying `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` are suppressed, currently only `MidTurnPrecheckSignal`
- [x] Real errors (without sentinel) still trigger normal error handling — regression proof included above
- [x] The sentinel uses a generic `agent-core.controlFlowError` name owned by the agent-core package
- [x] The check is scoped to `Agent.handleRunFailure` only (production path); removed from `agent-loop.ts` EventStream API
- [x] No breaking API changes, no new dependencies
- [x] JSDoc contract documentation in agent.ts
- [x] Gateway compilation verified (`pnpm dev gateway` builds and loads successfully)

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators can get stuck in a gateway restart death-loop for the same wedged main session. After the gateway restarts, the persisted aborted session can keep entering automatic restart recovery instead of being stopped once repeated automatic recovery has already shown that the session is wedged.

The user-visible failure mode is repeated automatic main-session resume across gateway boots, which keeps the gateway focused on the same wedged session instead of leaving the row in a terminal state for operator inspection.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the durable stop-condition direction from the existing PR, but changes the policy to the maintainer-requested recovery-fuse model rather than a generic cross-boot retry counter:

- Main-session restart recovery now has its own optional `mainRestartRecovery` state, aligned with the existing subagent tombstone shape: `automaticAttempts`, `lastAttemptAt`, `lastRunId`, `wedgedAt`, and `wedgedReason`.
- Only accepted automatic resume dispatches charge the durable fuse. Transcript preflight failures, transcript read failures, and dispatch-before-acceptance failures do not consume the fuse.
- Two rapid accepted automatic recovery attempts within two minutes are allowed; the next rapid re-entry tombstones the row before dispatch, clears `abortedLastRun`, and transitions the session to `failed` with terminal timing fields.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` stays a lifecycle-generation ignore list. For old released rows that only have repeated `restartRecoveryRuns` markers, recovery uses those markers only as a conservative compatibility floor, not as the canonical counter.
- The existing in-process `MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES` remains a transient startup retry/backoff guard and is no longer the durable cross-boot policy.

Boundaries and non-goals:

- The new persisted state is optional and scoped to automatic main-session restart recovery; existing rows do not need migration.
- This does not change credentials, auth, provider discovery, network behavior, public config defaults, wire protocol, Telegram/systemd runtime behavior, or lifecycle event suppression semantics.
- This does not add a new full Telegram/systemd/live-provider loop proof in this local environment. The PR already carries the prior Mantis Telegram Desktop gateway-run proof from the PR discussion, and this update adds issue-specific file-backed runtime proof through the production restart-recovery entrypoint.
- Another open candidate was visible for the same issue; this update repairs the existing contributor PR and leaves final landing-path choice to maintainers.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable automatic recovery stop condition across gateway restarts. A wedged main session can make two rapid accepted automatic recovery attempts, but the next rapid restart tombstones the row instead of repeatedly dispatching another resume. Deterministic transcript failures fail before charging that liveness fuse, so a bad transcript tail is not retried as if it were a transient gateway dispatch problem.

After inspection, `openclaw doctor --fix` can clear stale aborted recovery flags without deleting the tombstone metadata.

## Evidence

Issue-specific runtime proof through the production main-session restart-recovery entrypoint:

```text
Validation `post-commit-runtime-restart-recovery-tombstone-proof` (pass, exit_code=0)
```

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

Fixes #88330

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) introduced `allowBootstrap: true` in heartbeat delivery-target resolution so plugin channel targets could be loaded on demand. However, `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause

`bootstrapAttempts` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts`:
- **Success**: key cached → subsequent ticks skip
- **Failure** (plugin not installed / config issue): key deleted → every tick re-scans

## Changes

1. **Hot path**: heartbeat call sites pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`
2. **Startup pre-activation**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` loads external plugins once before heartbeat loop
3. **Per-agent coverage**: iterates `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` merge semantics)
4. **Session-derived `target:last`**: keeps guarded bootstrap (not pre-activatable from config)
5. **Hot reload & override preactivation**: `updateConfig` and `requestHeartbeat` (cron/manual wakes) call preactivation so externally-configured targets introduced after startup are covered
6. **Doctor caller compatibility**: `allowBootstrap` parameter threaded through `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` so doctor (which runs outside the wake loop) can resolve external plugin targets without preactivation
7. **Test coverage**: mock-backed assertions in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` verifying external-target resolution, standard-channel skip, dedup, and distinct-target branches

## Evidence

### Test proof

```
pnpm test src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
```
131/131 tests pass across 3 test files (19 + 87 + 25).

### Real gateway proof

Production config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`), heartbeat `every=30s target=qqbot`, no `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` — real gateway process with qqbot/feishu channels connected.

Gateway startup:
```
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] http server listening (12 plugins…)
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] ready
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [heartbeat] started
```

Proof event timeline (appendFileSync probes, reverted from source before commit):
```
[gateway]  pre-activate: target=qqbot isExternal=false  → standard channel no-op 1ms
[heartbeat] main-plugin resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] session-route resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] TICK COMPLETE: agent=test_agent channel=qqbot to=proof-test-target totalMs=3
```

## Revision (2026-07-06)

Addressed ClawSweeper review findings:

- **P1 — reload gap**: `updateConfig()` in heartbeat runner now calls `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` before rebuilding the agent schedule
- **P1 — override gap**: `requestHeartbeat()` wake handler pre-activates requested-heartbeat override targets before the no-bootstrap resolver runs
- **P1 — doctor regression**: `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` accepts `allowBootstrap?: boolean` so the doctor path (which runs outside the wake loop without preactivation) can still resolve external plugin targets
- **Test assertions**: `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` now uses mocked `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` with real assertions (call count, `allowBootstrap: true`, standard-channel skip, dedup)
- Kept existing `target:last` guarded bootstrap unchanged

## Revision (2026-07-07) #1

Removed duplicate heartbeat plugin preactivation path identified by ClawSweeper review:

- **P2 — duplicate startup preactivation**: Removed `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` from `activateGatewayScheduledServices`. The `startHeartbeatRunner` constructor already calls `updateConfig(state.cfg)` which handles the initial preactivation plus all hot-reload/config-update paths. Removing the gateway-side call eliminates a repeated registry scan when an external target fails to load.
- Updated comment in `heartbeat-runner.ts` `updateConfig` to reflect it is now the single preactivation path.
- 147 related tests pass (`server-runtime-services.test.ts`, `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, `targets.test.ts`).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #2 (a0ba292)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — gating preactivation to enabled, deliverable heartbeat configs:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` was called from `updateConfig` before the interval filter (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs`). A disabled heartbeat config (`every: "0m"`) with an external target still triggered `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` during startup/reload, scanning all installed plugins unnecessarily. External targets without a recipient (`to`) were also preactivated even though the runner can never deliver to them.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Config-scan path (startup/reload): each target is only preactivated when the heartbeat is enabled (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` returns non-null) AND has a deliverable recipient (`to` is set). This mirrors the `updateConfig` scheduling loop which skips agents with `intervalMs === 0`.
- Direct heartbeat override path (cron/manual wakes via `requestHeartbeat`): still preactivates without an interval check because the caller already validated the wake is active. Only skips targets without a recipient.

**New regression tests** (+7 in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`):
- ✅ Disabled default (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Disabled per-agent (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on default target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on per-agent target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on heartbeat override → no preactivation
- ✅ Per-agent with its own `every: "15m"` overrides disabled default → preactivated

**Test results**: 19/19 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass.

## Revision (2026-07-07) #3 (1334dd29)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — skip default target preactivation when explicit per-agent heartbeats override scheduling:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` unconditionally added `agents.defaults.heartbeat` to the target set even when `agents.list[]` entries had their own heartbeat configs. In that case `resolveHeartbeatAgents` schedules only the merged per-agent entries — it does not schedule the default as a standalone target. Preactivating the unused default target caused an unnecessary full-plugin-registry scan on startup/reload.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Added a `hasExplicitAgents` check mirroring `resolveHeartbeatAgents`: when any `agents.list[]` entry has a `heartbeat` block, the standalone default target is skipped. Only the per-agent effective targets (which may merge `target` or `to` from defaults) are preactivated.
- When no agent has an explicit heartbeat, the default target is still preactivated as before (it is what the scheduler runs).

**Updated tests** (+1 new regression, 2 existing tests adjusted):
- ✅ New: "skips the default external target when a per-agent heartbeat overrides it" — default `unused-external-plugin` with `to: room:default` is not preactivated because agent `override-agent` has its own `background-channel` target
- ✅ Adjusted: "pre-activates distinct external targets from defaults and per-agent configs" → now expects only the per-agent target (default skipped)
- ✅ Adjusted: "pre-activates a per-agent external target that inherits to from defaults" → now expects only the per-agent target with inherited `to` (default skipped)

**Test results**: 21/21 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass (133 total).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #4 — fix external-target detector (9db74edf)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — `isExternalPluginTarget` used wrong helper semantics:

**Problem**: `isExternalPluginTarget` used `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` and inverted its return value to decide "external plugin." But `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` preserves unknown plugin ids as deliverable (for external-plugin routing), so an explicit external target like `external-channel` made the helper return a truthy value and `isExternalPluginTarget` returned `false` — silently skipping bootstrap preactivation for external plugin targets.

**Root cause in the contract**:
- `normalizeMessageChannel` (in `message-channel-core.ts:27`) preserves unknown-but-normalized ids: `return normalizeAnyChannelId(normalized) ?? normalized`
- `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` wraps `normalizeMessageChannel` + `isDeliverableMessageChannel`, so it returns a truthy value for unknown external plugin channels
- The old `isExternalPluginTarget` inverted this: `return !normalized` — wrong, because the helper returned a value for external channels

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Replaced `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` + `normalizeChatChannelId`
- `isDeliverableMessageChannel(rawTarget)` confirms the target is a deliverable channel id (non-internal, non-empty)
- `!normalizeChatChannelId(rawTarget)` confirms it's NOT a built-in chat channel — built-in channels are already in the bundled catalog and don't need bootstrap
- Only targets that pass both checks (deliverable but not built-in) are classified as external plugin targets

**Updated tests** — `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`:
- Replaced `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` mock with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` + `normalizeChatChannelId` mocks
- `isDeliverableMessageChannel` now returns `true` for any non-empty string (matching real contract: unknown plugin ids are deliverable)
- `normalizeChatChannelId` only returns non-null for built-in channel ids (`telegram`, `discord`, `whatsapp`)
- This means external plugin targets (e.g. `external-channel`) correctly pass `isExternalPluginTarget` — deliverable but not built-in → needs preactivation
- Built-in channel targets (e.g. `telegram`) correctly fail `isExternalPluginTarget` — deliverable AND built-in → skip preactivation

**Test results**: 22/22 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass (136 total).



## Revision (2026-07-08)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — explicit normalized heartbeat plugin targets not honoring caller `allowBootstrap`:

**Problem**: When `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` preserves an external plugin channel id (production normalization contract at `message-channel-core.ts:27-29`), the explicit target reaches the later plugin lookup at `targets.ts:217-225`. That lookup hardcoded `allowBootstrap: isSessionDerived` (always `false` for explicit targets) and `allowBundledFallback: !isSessionDerived` (always `true` for explicit targets). This meant:
- Doctor's `allowBootstrap: true` was ignored → false "replies are dropped silently" warnings for external plugin heartbeat targets
- Bundled fallback was enabled on the heartbeat hot path → could lazy-load bundled channel module code contrary to the performance boundary

**Fix in `targets.ts`**:
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget`: plugin lookup now honors `params.allowBootstrap` for explicit targets (`isSessionDerived || params.allowBootstrap === true`) and disables bundled fallback unconditionally (`allowBundledFallback: false`)
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTargetWithSessionRoute`: bundled fallback also disabled in sync with the primary resolution path

**New regression tests** (+2 in `targets.test.ts`):
- ✅ Doctor `allowBootstrap: true` passes through for explicit external targets preserved by production normalization
- ✅ Hot path keeps `allowBootstrap: false` with bundled fallback disabled
- Both tests override the normalization mock to simulate production behavior where external plugin ids are preserved (rather than returning `undefined`)

**Test results**: 89/89 `targets.test.ts`, 22/22 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, 7/7 `doctor-heartbeat-session-target.test.ts` — all pass (145 total).


## Revision (2026-07-08) #2 — fix CI lint (9a37f344)

Fixed `check-lint` CI failure (2 `eslint/curly` violations in `targets.test.ts`):

**Problem**: Two newly added test helpers in revision #1 used single-line `if (cond) return val;` without braces — a style rule enforced by `eslint/curly` in CI.

**Fix in `targets.test.ts`**: Added braces to both `if` statements (lines 987, 1026):
```ts
if (normalized === "ext-plugin") {
  return normalized;
}
```

**Test results**: 145/145 pass across 4 test files. `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean.

target.title: fix(browser): bound Chrome launch stderr diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Fixes an issue where users could hit Chrome launch failures or stuck startup while OpenClaw retained the entire Chrome launch stderr stream in memory before diagnostics were rendered.**
- **Affected surface / workflow:** Managed Chrome startup in `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts`, specifically the launch path that waits for CDP readiness and includes stderr diagnostics when startup fails.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The original PR correctly moved stderr retention toward a bounded 64 KiB launch buffer, but the retained tail became the only source for stale Singleton-lock recovery, missing-display/profile-lock hints, and final rendered diagnostics. Early recovery markers could roll out of the tail, the displayed 2,000 characters came from the start of the retained tail instead of the newest failure output, and byte trimming could start inside a UTF-8 character.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Chrome startup failures should keep OpenClaw memory bounded without regressing existing retry/hint behavior or showing stale/malformed diagnostics. Users still need the latest redacted Chrome failure output plus existing recovery guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** The launch path now stores stderr through a bounded diagnostics accumulator: it keeps the 64 KiB byte tail for redacted display, tracks recovery/hint signals while chunks stream, renders the newest display slice with `slice(-CHROME_STDERR_HINT_MAX_CHARS)`, and drops leading continuation bytes before UTF-8 decoding so diagnostics do not start with replacement characters after a boundary trim.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The memory bound remains at the stderr collection boundary, while the downstream behavior that previously depended on the full stderr stream now has independent bounded state for the facts it needs. This fixes the correctness regressions instead of widening the retained buffer or adding an after-the-fact fallback.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** `launchOpenClawChrome` remains the owner of managed-Chrome launch diagnostics and retry decisions. target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): metrics and logs posted to the traces endpoint when the shared OTLP endpoint is signal-qualified
target.body:
Closes #98886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configuring a single shared OTLP `endpoint` that ends in a signal path (e.g. a hosted frontend URL such as `https://host/api/public/otel/v1/traces`) would have **metrics and logs POSTed to the traces endpoint** when more than one signal was enabled. OTLP backends then reject the wrong wire type (Langfuse logs `invalid wire type 7`), so metrics and logs never arrive.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveOtelUrl` now normalizes only the *shared* endpoint: when it already ends in `/v1/<signal>`, the trailing segment is rewritten to match the signal being resolved (`/v1/traces` -> `/v1/metrics` or `/v1/logs`), preserving any query string or fragment. Explicit per-signal overrides (`*Endpoint` config and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT` env) are still used verbatim, and bare base URLs keep the existing append behavior — so no currently-working configuration changes.

This is the same design as the open #98911 (and the closed #98899 / #98915). A fresh PR is opened because #98911 has been stale since Jul 2 (merge-conflicting, all CI checks cancelled, not mergeable) with no maintainer activity. Happy to close this in favor of a rebased #98911 if a maintainer prefers — the goal is just to land a correct, mergeable, green fix. This PR also adds a docs note and a regression test that fails on the unfixed code.

## User Impact

Operators can point a single shared `endpoint` at a signal-qualified OTLP URL and have traces, metrics, and logs each delivered to the correct path, without needing per-signal `*Endpoint` overrides.

## Evidence

- New regression test `normalizes a shared signal-qualified endpoint for the other signals` (shared `.../v1/traces?timeout=30s`, traces + metrics + logs): traces unchanged, metrics -> `.../v1/metrics?timeout=30s`, logs -> `.../v1/logs?timeout=30s`. Verified it **fails on the pre-fix source** (metric URL resolved to `.../v1/traces`) and passes after.
- New lock-in test `preserves an explicit per-signal signal-qualified endpoint verbatim` guards the preserve path against future over-normalization.
- `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`: **108 passed** (`vitest.extension-misc.config.ts`); `oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug (showing "accounts 1" when the correct value is `0`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

### Control-flow proof

```
accounts.length === 0
  → anyEnabled = [].some(a => a.enabled) === false       (line 283)
  → !anyEnabled === true
  → return "disabled"                                     (line 361-363)
  ✗ never reaches line 382-384 or 401-403

enabledAccounts.length === 0
  → configuredAccounts = [].filter(...) === []            (line 285)
  → configuredAccounts.length === 0
  → line 418 guard fails
  ✗ never reaches line 423
```

### Why This Change Is Justified (Benefits)

- **消除维护隐患（Maintenance Hazard）**：保留 `|| 1` 會給未來的程式碼閱讀者一個錯誤的暗示——「這裡的長度有可能為 0」。如果以後有人重構了前置的守衛條件（Guard Condition），可能就會誤以為有這個兜底而引發隱藏的 Bug。
- **明確程式碼不變量（Invariant）**：移除冗餘代碼後，邏輯更加乾淨，不變量（此處長度必然大於 0）變得直觀顯性。
- **零運行風險（Zero Regression Risk）**：提交者已經在本地環境（Node v24.13.1）執行了單元測試 `pnpm test src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts` 且全部通過，並且通過靜態掃描工具 `oxlint` 證實沒有引入任何新錯誤。這是一次非常標準且高質量的代碼優化（Cleanup）。

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. This is purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — renderer invariant verification (real `node --import tsx` output):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
// Prove: for every input that reaches the three changed expressions,
// accounts.length (or enabledAccounts.length) is guaranteed >= 1.

// 1. The !anyEnabled guard (line 361) catches accounts.length === 0
const emptyAccts = [];
const anyEnabledEmpty = emptyAccts.some(a => a.enabled);
console.log('accounts=[] → anyEnabled:', anyEnabledEmpty,
            '→ guard fires:', !anyEnabledEmpty);
console.log('  Line 361: if (!anyEnabled) return \"disabled\";');
console.log('  → accounts.length=0 NEVER reaches lines 382-403');

// 2. configuredAccounts ⊆ enabledAccounts (line 285, 418)
console.log('');
console.log('configuredAccounts = enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured);');
console.log('→ subset relation: |configured| ≤ |enabled| always');
console.log('→ |configured|>0 ⇒ |enabled|≥1 ⇒ || 1 is dead code');

// 3. After-fix rendering: accounts.length=1 with forceAccountBinding
const acc = [{enabled: true, configured: true}];
console.log('');
console.log('accounts.length=1 + forceAccountBinding:');
console.log('  accounts \${acc.length||1} =', \`accounts \${acc.length || 1}\`);
console.log('  accounts \${acc.length}    =', \`accounts \${acc.length}\`);
console.log('  ✅ identical — zero regression risk');
"
```
```
accounts=[] → anyEnabled: false → guard fires: true
  Line 361: if (!anyEnabled) return "disabled";
  → accounts.length=0 NEVER reaches lines 382-403

configuredAccounts = enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured);
→ subset relation: |configured| ≤ |enabled| always
→ |configured|>0 ⇒ |enabled|≥1 ⇒ || 1 is dead code

accounts.length=1 + forceAccountBinding:
  accounts ${acc.length||1} = accounts 1
  accounts ${acc.length}    = accounts 1
  ✅ identical — zero regression risk
```

**Proof 2 — Vitest suite on the changed module (PR head, Node v24.13.1):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Start at  09:34:21
   Duration  7.16s
```

**Observed result after fix:** The renderer invariant proof confirms that `accounts.length` and `enabledAccounts.length` are structurally guaranteed to be ≥ 1 at all three evaluation points. The 9 existing regression tests pass unchanged, confirming no behavioral regression.

**What was not tested:** The `channels-token-summary.ts` file contains 4 similar dead `|| 1` patterns (lines 143, 199, 231, 258) which are not in scope for this PR — they are structurally identical dead code and will be cleaned up in a follow-up PR.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 9 tests passed** ✅
- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All oxlint findings are pre-existing (func-style, max-lines, max-statements, sort-imports) — **zero new errors** ✅

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`:

- **Lines 383/402** (`accounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (accounts.length > 1 || plugin.meta.forceAccountBinding)` branch is never reached when `accounts.length === 0` because `!anyEnabled` (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before the `link.statusState` block is entered.
- **Line 423** (`enabledAccounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (configuredAccounts.length > 0)` (line 418) ensures `configuredAccounts.length >= 1`. Since `configuredAccounts` is computed as `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), the subset relation guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length >= 1`.

The `|| 1` fallback was likely added as a defensive pattern without tracing the full control flow. Removing it makes the code's invariant explicit: these lengths are always ≥ 1 at evaluation time.

target.title: fix(agents): do not mark exact-size streamed responses as truncated
target.body:
Closes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `web_fetch` reports a response body as truncated when the streamed response is exactly `maxResponseBytes` bytes long, even though no bytes were omitted. This produces a false "Response body truncated" warning and triggers unnecessary spill handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` treated `bytesRead >= maxBytes` as truncation. An exact-size stream already stops cleanly when the reader returns `done`, so the extra `>=` check was incorrect. The fix only sets `truncated` when an actual overflow chunk is seen.

## User Impact

Users no longer see a truncation warning for web_fetch responses that exactly fit the configured byte limit.

## Evidence

Added a focused regression test in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` that streams two chunks totaling exactly the `maxBytes` limit and expects `truncated: false`.

Before the fix, the new test fails:

```
FAIL  |agents| src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts > readResponseText > does not flag a response whose stream ends exactly at the byte limit as truncated
AssertionError: expected { text: 'hello world', …(2) } to deeply equal { text: 'hello world', …(2) }
- Expected
+ Received
  {
    "bytesRead": 11,
    "text": "hello world",
-   "truncated": false,
+   "truncated": true,
  }
```

After the fix, the test passes, and the existing truncation test still passes:

```
✓ |agents| src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts (12 tests)
✓ |agents| tools/web-fetch.test.ts (14 tests)
✓ |agents| tools/web-tools.fetch.test.ts (28 tests)
```

target.title: feat(android): bind app chat to a dedicated session
target.body:
Related: #45854

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Android app chat could reuse the gateway's generic main session context after pairing, so app-originated chat history and follow-up requests were not cleanly isolated from other OpenClaw surfaces connected to the same agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android app now derives a stable `openclaw-app-*` session key for each connected gateway endpoint, explicitly creates that app session after a successful operator connection, and binds chat/history/talk mode to that key before app chat traffic resumes.

The app session create request intentionally omits parent-session and emit-hook fields, so the Android app session is independent rather than a child of another surface. The proof workflow is manual-only behind `workflow_dispatch` + `include_android`, so normal push/PR CI does not run the emulator media capture by default.

## User Impact

Android app users get a dedicated OpenClaw App session per gateway connection. Reconnects and gateway switches keep app chat scoped to the Android app's session instead of blending into the agent's default `main` chat or other connected surfaces.

## Evidence

- Full CI run passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28907001143
- Android app session media proof job passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28907001143/job/85758758496
- Media/log artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28907001143/artifacts/8154958242

The artifact contains:

- `openclaw-app-session-proof.mp4` and `openclaw-app-session-proof.png` from a real Android emulator run.
- `session-create.json` showing the app created `agent:main:openclaw-app-1f52fae09049` with label `OpenClaw App · Proof Pixel`.
- `gateway-events.jsonl` showing `sessions.create` followed by `chat.history` using the same app session key.
- `logcat-tail.txt` and the debug APK used for the emulator proof.

Relevant captured `sessions.create` payload:

```json

  "method": "sessions.create",
  "key": "agent:main:openclaw-app-1f52fae09049",
  "label": "OpenClaw App · Proof Pixel",
  "agentId": "main",
  "hasParentSessionKey": false,
  "hasEmitCommandHooks": false
```

Local lightweight checks run before pushing:

- `git diff --check`
- `ruby -e "require 'yaml'; YAML.load_file('.github/workflows/ci.yml', aliases: true); puts 'ci yaml ok'"`
- `pnpm native:i18n:check`

## Evidence Source Map

- Dedicated Android app session key: `session-create.json` from the media proof artifact.
- App chat binding to the dedicated session: `gateway-events.jsonl` shows `chat.history` with the same `agent:main:openclaw-app-*` key.
- No child-session coupling: `session-create.json` records `hasParentSessionKey: false` and `hasEmitCommandHooks: false`.
- Real UI/media evidence: emulator screenshot and MP4 in the uploaded artifact.
- CI coverage: successful run `28907001143` at the exact PR head SHA.

## Risk

- Low runtime risk: the session key is derived from the gateway endpoint/device identity and remains stable across reconnects.
- The change touches Android session binding and chat history routing; tests cover key generation and chat controller session policy.
- The emulator proof job is manual-only and pinned to full action SHAs.

## Rollback

Revert this PR to return Android chat to the previous gateway main-session behavior and remove the manual emulator proof job.

target.title: fix(browser): handle Chrome launch stderr pipe errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts:launchOpenClawChrome` spawns Chrome with
`stdio: ["ignore", "ignore", "pipe"]` and attaches a `proc.stderr.on("data", ...)`
listener that buffers stderr chunks for launch-failure diagnostics. The listener
is registered and detached cleanly, but **no `error` listener is attached to
`proc.stderr`**. If the stderr pipe emits an `EPIPE` / `RST` (e.g. Chrome's
parent already exited and the kernel tore the pipe down before Chrome's own
exit handler ran), Node escalates the `error` event to an unhandled error that
crashes the gateway host — even though the child process itself is on its way
out and the launch-failure path would handle it correctly.

This is the same class of bug Alix-007 / cxbAsDev / steipete have been
canonically fixing across `file-transfer` (#101590), `discord` ffmpeg (#101124),
`google-meet` audio bridge (#101596, open), `matrix` deps (#101597, open),
`microsoft-foundry` az login (#101598, open), and `codex-supervisor` stdio
(#101599, open). It is a transport-layer unhandled-error family that Node
explicitly warns about, and the pattern is well-validated against the canonical
`proc.stderr.on("error", (err) => log.warn(...))` fix.

## Changes

- `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts`: import `formatErrorMessage`
  from `../infra/errors.js` and register a `proc.stderr.on("error", ...)`
  listener in `launchOnceAndWait`, immediately after the existing
  `proc.stderr.on("data", onStderr)` registration. The listener logs the
  pipe failure via `log.warn` and lets the existing launch-readiness
  kill / diagnostic flow continue.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts`: add a focused
  regression test that emits a synthetic `EPIPE` on the fake Chrome stderr
  stream after `launchOpenClawChrome` has registered its `error` listener.
  The test asserts that the launch-failure path still resolves with
  `/Failed to start Chrome CDP/` and that `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` was called.

This is the **symmetric counterpart to** the active stream-error campaign
PRs (#101590 #101124 #101596 #101597 #101598 #101599). It is **not** a
duplicate of #101506 (`mikasa0818`, "bound Chrome launch stderr diagnostics")
which fixes a *different* dimension — bounded 64 KiB tail retention at
the collection boundary. The two fixes are orthogonal: bounded-buffer
caps in-memory growth; this PR prevents unhandled-error crashes when the
pipe itself fails.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Chrome launch with a pipe failure on the stderr
  stream must not crash the gateway host. The launch-failure diagnostic
  path must still resolve, the child must be SIGKILL'd, and the failure
  must be reported via `log.warn`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0,
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against the production launch path with
  `child_process.spawn` mocked.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts -t "does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch"`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` (full file)
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
   ✓ chrome.ts internal > launchOpenClawChrome > does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed | 54 skipped (55)
     Start at  08:51:26
     Duration  16.67s
  ```
  Full file:
  ```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  55 passed (55)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: The fixture EventEmitter starts with no
  `error` listener. The test hooks `fakeProc.stderr.on("newListener", ...)`
  to wait until `launchOpenClawChrome` has attached the production
  listener, then emits `new Error("EPIPE")` on stderr. The production
  listener routes the event through `log.warn`, the launch-readiness
  loop times out, `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` fires, and `launchOpenClawChrome`
  rejects with `Failed to start Chrome CDP on port 55558 for profile
  "openclaw-launch-XXXX". CDP diagnostic: http_unreachable after 2000ms;
  cdp=http://127.0.0.1:55558; ECONNREFUSED.` — matching the canonical
  sibling-fix shape.
- **Negative control** (proves the test exercises the fix, not a
  tautology): reverting only the `chrome.ts` change while keeping the
  new test makes the test time out at the 120s vitest default — the
  `error` event has no listener and Node escalates it to an unhandled
  crash that the test cannot recover from:
  ```
  $ timeout 130 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...
  (terminated, exit 124)
  ```
- **What was not tested**:
  - Real Chrome process under controlled stderr EPIPE conditions (would
    require a daemonized Chrome + parent-exit harness; out of scope for
    a transport-layer listener fix).
  - Live CI on `openclaw/main` (the PR is pre-push; CI verification is
    expected to run on push).

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Chrome launch must not crash the gateway host
  when the spawned Chrome child's stderr pipe fails with `EPIPE` /
  `RST`. The fix adds the missing `error` listener that mirrors the
  pattern Alix-007 / cxbAsDev / steipete have shipped across
  `file-transfer`, `discord` ffmpeg, `google-meet`, `matrix`,
  `microsoft-foundry`, and `codex-supervisor`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0,
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` driving `launchOpenClawChrome` with
  `child_process.spawn` mocked.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts -t "does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch"` → 1 passed
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → 55/55 passed
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → exit 0
  - `pnpm tsgo:extensions` → exit 0
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → All matched files use the correct format
- **Evidence after fix**: 55/55 vitest tests pass; new test
  "does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch"
  passes (8.51s start, 16.67s duration). Negative control confirms the
  test exercises the production listener by reverting it and observing
  the test time out at 120s with exit 124.
- **Observed result after fix**: Launch-failure path still resolves
  with `Failed to start Chrome CDP ... ECONNREFUSED`; `proc.kill("SIGKILL")`
  fires; `proc.stderr` `error` listener routes through `log.warn`.
- **What was not tested**: Real Chrome stderr-pipe EPIPE under controlled
  Chrome + parent-exit harness (out of scope for a transport-layer
  listener fix).

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` —
  **55/55 passed** (12.91s start, 22.06s duration)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on changed files — exit 0

Added tests:

- `does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch` —
  drives `launchOpenClawChrome` with `child_process.spawn` mocked,
  waits for the production `error` listener to attach (via the
  `EventEmitter.newListener` hook), emits a synthetic `EPIPE` on
  the fake stderr stream, and asserts that the launch-failure path
  still resolves with `/Failed to start Chrome CDP/` and that
  `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` fires. The test inverts to a 120s timeout
  when the production fix is reverted, proving the assertion exercises
  the new listener rather than a tautology.

## Risk checklist

- **Scope**: 2 files, 1 module (`chrome.ts:launchOpenClawChrome`); +11 prod, +53 test.
- **Behavior**: Old launch path unchanged. Only addition is the
  `error` listener on `proc.stderr`, which logs and lets the existing
  recovery flow continue.
- **API/signature changes**: none.
- **Type check**: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` exit 0.
- **Sibling PRs**: This is the **chrome.ts counterpart** to the active
  stream-error campaign: #101590 (file-transfer), #101124 (discord ffmpeg),
  #101596 (google-meet), #101597 (matrix), #101598 (microsoft-foundry),
  #101599 (codex-supervisor). It is **not** a duplicate of #101506
  (`mikasa0818`, "bound Chrome launch stderr diagnostics") which fixes a
  different dimension (bounded 64 KiB buffer tail vs stream `error`
  listener).

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)

- The `bootstrap` spawn inside `launchOpenClawChrome` (line 1001) does
  not register a stderr `data` listener at all and is therefore not
  affected by the same `error`-listener gap; no change is required
  there. If a follow-up PR wants belt-and-braces coverage on the
  bootstrap path it can land independently.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in az login
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers for interactive `az login --use-device-code`
- align the stream-error path with the established `src/node-host/invoke.ts` lifecycle pattern: record the first stream error, send one SIGTERM, escalate to SIGKILL after a grace period, and settle from the child `close` event (with a bounded fallback for shells that never emit `close`)
- keep duplicate stream errors and late child `error` events idempotent: the first stream error wins and teardown runs once
- cover the lifecycle with mocked-timer regressions plus a real spawned local `az` substitute process over real stdio pipes
- collision check: no open PR found for the Microsoft Foundry az login stream-error issue or `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts`

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` — passed; 1 file, 2 tests passed (real local child-process proof)
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- mutation check: forcing the stream error to reject immediately (before child close) made both real-process tests fail on the close-before-rejection assertions; reverting the mutation made the same focused tests pass

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Foundry `az login --use-device-code` stdout/stderr stream errors are contained without an unhandled stream error, duplicate teardown, or settlement before the child closes.
Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; the proof uses a PATH-injected local `az` substitute executable — a real spawned process with real stdio pipes, not the Azure CLI and not an in-process mocked child.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`.
Evidence after fix: `[proof] local az substitute pid=3820935 forced stdout stream error contained; close observed before rejection` and `[proof] local az substitute pid=3820960 ignored SIGTERM; SIGKILL escalation closed child before rejection`; `Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 2 passed (2)`.
Observed result after fix: the first forced stdout stream error is reported as `az login stdout stream failed`, duplicate stderr stream errors are ignored, the promise does not reject before child `close`, and a SIGTERM-ignoring substitute is escalated to SIGKILL before rejection.
What was not tested: a live Azure CLI/device-code authentication and a kernel-originated stdout read error — Node offers no reliable local way to force a kernel read error on `child.stdout`, so the test drives the real exported function with a real child process and forces the Node stream error on that real pipe.
